beats.narration_en: How do you stop a jet doing a hundred fifty miles an hour?
The deck is far too short to brake, so the jet drops a hook.
It snags one of four steel cables stretched across the deck.
Below deck, the cable runs around pulleys to a giant hydraulic piston.
As the jet drags the cable out, the piston forces oil through a valve, turning speed into heat.
It stops a fifty-thousand-pound jet in about the length of a football field.
The pilot hits full throttle anyway, in case the hook misses.
That's me in the cockpit, by the way.
And after a hundred twenty-five landings, the cable gets thrown away.
